statement.text:
Groups A and B are said to be locally equivalent if for every finitely generated
subgroup X ⩽ A there is a subgroup Y ⩽ B isomorphic to X, and conversely, for
every finitely generated subgroup Y ⩽ B there is a subgroup X ⩽ A, isomorphic
to Y . We call a group G categorical if G is isomorphic to any group that is locally
equivalent to G. Is it true that a periodic locally soluble group G is categorical if and
only if G is hyperfinite with Chernikov Sylow subgroups? (A group is hyperfinite if
it has a well ordered ascending normal series with finite factors.)        V. V. Belyaev
